doc.title: Bill Charlap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: His trio with Kenny Washington and Peter Washington
summary: He has played two and a half years with the two Washingtons, whose natural connection needs little discussion.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You have a crew of musicians that you like to call in your own trio now?

Well my trio is Kenny Washington and Peter Washington. And we’ve been playing together for the last two and a half years or so. And there’s a very natural connection between us, a very natural feeling about what we care about, what are the central forces that we — just a sort of center current to the things we care about musically, that’s all. And we don’t really need to discuss very much. We never have. The approach happens very naturally. Both guys have great command, great understanding of their instruments historically, and are very analytical as well. However, it’s all about feeling and feeling first. So with all of that it allows us to cover a lot of ground.
